relevance_reason: A population GWAS in FinnGen found a recessive association between a Finnish-enriched TBPL2 stop-gained variant (p.Arg299Ter) and female infertility, with homozygous women having markedly fewer offspring. This adds evidence for the TBPL2-related oocyte maturation arrest entry, although no oocyte phenotyping was done.

findings.statement: In a genomewide association study of 22,849 Finnish women with infertility and 198,989 control women who had given birth, from the FinnGen cohort, Ruotsalainen et al. (2024) used a recessive model and identified a genome-wide significant association with a stop-gained variant in TBPL2, rs144313315 (c.895A>T, p.Arg299Ter; NM_199047.3). The odds ratio was 650.1 (p = 4.11 x 10(-25)). The variant introduces a premature stop codon in the DNA-binding part of the protein, was predicted to cause loss of function with a CADD score of 40, and was associated only with infertility and no other diseases.
quotes: The strongest association was observed in the recessive analysis at the TBPL2 locus on chromosome 14 with an odds ratio (OR) of 650.1 (p = 4.11 × 10−25).

The mutation introduces a premature stop codon (p.Arg299Ter) in the DNA-binding part of the protein predicted to be a high-confidence predicted loss-of-function variant (pLOF) with a Combined Annotation Dependent Depletion (CADD) score of 40
In our follow-up analyses, the TBPL2 mutation was associated only with infertility and no other diseases.

findings.statement: Ruotsalainen et al. (2024) found that women homozygous for the TBPL2 p.Arg299Ter variant had significantly fewer offspring, an average of 0.16 compared with 1.75 in the other genotype groups (p = 1.4 x 10(-15)). Of 41 homozygous women, only 4 had given birth. All 4 had undergone IVF therapy; whether donor oocytes were used was not known. The authors concluded that the variant is associated with a rather severe form of infertility.
quotes: individuals carrying two copies of that variant having significantly fewer offspring (average of 0.16) compared to women belonging to the other genotype groups (average of 1.75 offspring, p = 1.4 × 10-15)

two out of 41 individuals carrying two copies of the risk allele had given birth to one child, whereas two individuals carrying two copies of the risk allele had given birth to more than one child. All four women had undergone IVF therapy, although more detailed information on the potential use of donor oocytes is not available.
These data indicate that the TPBL2 c.895A>T (p.Arg299Ter) variant is associated with a rather severe form of infertility.

findings.statement: Ruotsalainen et al. (2024) reported that the TBPL2 p.Arg299Ter variant has a minor allele frequency of 1.1% in Finland and is 43 times more frequent there than in non-Finnish Europeans. It is distributed fairly evenly across Finland, with regional allele frequencies of 0.84% to 2.38%. In gnomAD, loss-of-function variants in TBPL2 are rare, with this variant as the exception.
quotes: is a rare stop-gained mutation (p.Arg299Ter, minor-allele frequency [MAF]: 1.1% in Finland) that is highly enriched to Finland (43 times compared to non-Finnish Europeans). The variant appears rather evenly distributed across Finland, with an allele frequency range of 0.84%–2.38% (Figure S8).
According to data from gnomAD (v.3.1.2), loss-of-function mutations in TBPL2 are rare, with the stop-gained mutation associated with infertility in this study being an exception.

findings.statement: Ruotsalainen et al. (2024) found that the TBPL2 locus acts recessively: the proportion of women with infertility was significantly higher only among those carrying two copies of the effect allele. The TBPL2 association was seen uniformly in both early-onset and late-onset infertility.
quotes: These data confirm that both the PKHD1L1 and TBPL2 loci exhibit a recessive mode of action, i.e., the proportion of affected individuals with infertility is significantly elevated only among individuals carrying two copies of the effect allele.
Some loci, such as TBPL2, are uniformly associated with infertility in both early- and late-onset affected individuals

relevance_reason: Reports an infertile woman with impaired folliculogenesis and failed oocyte retrieval who carries compound heterozygous TBPL2 variants, the gene for OZEMA29.

findings.statement: Du et al. (2023) reported a 32-year-old woman who had unexplained primary infertility for 10 years. Most of her basal hormone levels were roughly normal, but her basal FSH was elevated. Her anti-Mullerian hormone level was normal. Two attempts at oocyte collection had failed, which was consistent with impaired ovarian folliculogenesis and failure of superovulation.
quotes: A 32-year-old female was diagnosed with unexplained primary infertility for 10 years. She had roughly normal basal hormone levels, but her basal follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) levels were elevated.
the level of anti-Mullerian hormone was within the normal range, and she had undergone two failed oocyte collection attempts

phenotypes.hpo_label: Elevated circulating follicle stimulating hormone level

findings.statement: Du et al. (2023) carried out whole-exome sequencing on the patient, then confirmed the result by Sanger sequencing in her family. They identified compound heterozygous TBPL2 variants: a novel nonsense variant, c.802C>T (p.Arg268Ter), and a previously reported variant, c.788+3A>G (reported as p.Arg233Ter). They checked allele frequencies in ExAC and gnomAD and assessed pathogenicity with SIFT, MutationTaster, and CADD. The authors concluded that these variants caused the impaired ovarian folliculogenesis, failed superovulation, and infertility.
quotes: One novel mutation, c.802C > T (p. Arg268Ter), and one known variant, c.788 + 3A > G (p. Arg233Ter), in TBPL2 were identified in the infertile family.
Whole-exome sequencing was performed on the patient, and TBPL2 mutations were identified and confirmed by Sanger sequencing.
We identified compound heterozygous mutations in TBPL2 that caused impaired ovarian folliculogenesis, failure of superovulation, and infertility in patients.

relevance_reason: Reports a homozygous TBPL2 missense variant in two infertile sisters with oocyte maturation arrest, which defines OZEMA29.

findings.statement: Wang et al. (2021) described 2 infertile sisters from a consanguineous family who had female infertility caused by oocyte maturation arrest and degeneration.
quotes: in two infertile sisters with oocyte maturation arrest and degeneration from a consanguineous family by whole-exome sequencing

findings.statement: Wang et al. (2021) used whole-exome sequencing to identify a homozygous missense mutation in the TBPL2 gene (c.895T>C, p.C299R) in 2 infertile sisters from a consanguineous family who had oocyte maturation arrest and degeneration. The authors described the mutation as rare and pathogenic. Functional studies showed that it impaired the transcription initiation function of the protein.
quotes: we identified a homozygous missense mutation (c.895T>C; p.C299R) in TBPL2 (TATA box binding protein like 2) in two infertile sisters with oocyte maturation arrest and degeneration from a consanguineous family by whole-exome sequencing
The TBPL2 mutation is rare and pathogenic, and impaired the transcription initiation function of the protein.

relevance_reason: Reports a homozygous TBPL2 splice variant in two unrelated families with oocyte maturation defects and infertility, which establishes OZEMA29.

findings.statement: Yang et al. (2021) studied 2 unrelated families with female infertility caused by defects in oocyte maturation. The patients had repeated IVF failures, and only 2 immature metaphase I (MI) oocytes could be obtained from the patients.
quotes: Two infertile families characterized by oocyte maturation defects were recruited for whole-exome sequencing (WES).
only two immature MI oocytes were obtained from the patients

findings.statement: In affected women from 2 unrelated families with oocyte maturation defects and infertility, Yang et al. (2021) used whole-exome sequencing with Sanger confirmation to identify a homozygous splice site variant in the TBPL2 gene (c.788+3A>G). Haplotype analysis showed that the disease alleles in the 2 families arose independently. A minigene assay showed that the variant disrupted the integrity of TBPL2 mRNA.
quotes: A homozygous splicing variant (c.788 + 3A>G) in TBPL2 was identified in two unrelated families characterized by oocyte maturation defects.
Haplotype analysis indicated that the disease allele of Families 1 and 2 was independent. The variant disrupted the integrity of TBPL2 mRNA.

findings.statement: Yang et al. (2021) sequenced the transcriptome of affected oocytes carrying the TBPL2 variant and found that genes vital for oocyte maturation and fertilization were widely and markedly downregulated. They suggested that the mutation in the transcription factor TBPL2 led to global gene expression changes in oocytes.
quotes: Transcriptome sequencing of affected oocytes showed that vital genes for oocyte maturation and fertilization were widely and markedly downregulated, suggesting that a mutation in the transcriptional factor, TBPL2, led to global gene alterations in oocytes.

relevance_reason: The title reports a recurrent TBPL2 mutation causing female infertility with diminished ovarian reserve, which is the subject of OZEMA29. Only the title was available.

findings.statement: He et al. (2020) reported that a recurrent mutation in the TBPL2 gene caused diminished ovarian reserve and female infertility.
quotes: A recurrent mutation in TBPL2 causes diminished ovarian reserve and female infertility.
